agree.reason: The plain apology helps, but this household's real grievances were the silence and getting no credit, and the email promises nothing about either, so they would still have reason to doubt that a bad week would be handled differently.

honest.reason: Every fact matches the brief, and the nets are correctly limited to tomatoes and peppers; the only stretch is calling pause credit "paid pauses," which is mildly loose.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are only repeated, not worked: there is no per-week cost (about $24.50), and the $31,000 is never framed as money spent to protect members' boxes.

right_comparison.reason: It never says what this reader gets by staying away compared with returning under the new terms, and it never shows how a hail week would now play out differently from last July.

qualification.reason: It needed to say that crop loss can't be ruled out, paired with the checkable promise of credit when weather cuts a box by more than a third; it leaves both out, which quietly implies the risk has been fixed.

objections.reason: The objection "you went quiet and gave no credit" is met only with an apology: the weekly Thursday email and the weather credit, which answer it directly, are missing, and pause credit isn't a substitute.

fit.reason: It is an email of roughly 200 words, but the [Name], [Your name] and [Farm name] placeholders are left unfilled even though Sam Turner and Greenbank Farm were known, and the link doesn't say it's on the website.
